hens_rule_text: Up to 6 adult hens per lot, plus up to 6 non-egg-laying replacement chicks or pullets, but only with a Use of Premises live fowl permit from Inspectional Services and Zoning Board of Appeals approval.
permit_notes: A Use of Premises permit from Boston Inspectional Services is required under Article 89 of the Boston Zoning Code, including a plot plan, an inspection, and review by the Zoning Board of Appeals where abutters can comment.
setback_notes: Coops and runs must be at least 25 ft from neighboring dwellings.
coop_rules: Coop must be in the rear yard, fully enclosed, kept sanitary, no taller than 8 ft, and meet the setback from neighboring homes.
zoning_notes: Urban agriculture, including chicken keeping, is governed by Article 89 of the Boston Zoning Code, applied citywide but with abutter comment as part of the permit process.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
research_notes: The permit process, hen cap and rooster ban come from Boston's own Live Fowl Permit Information page (official city source, read via search extract); the 25 ft setback and 8 ft coop height are from secondary chicken-law summaries that align with the city page but could not be independently confirmed in the Article 89 text itself.
